tables.name: customers
tables.description: A business's record of one customer (FS line 727, the customer row), per business and person: the name the business has on file, the contact on file (a mobile and an optional email, as K-04 handles), the way they are reached, their contact preferences, their age band and the owner's fee-free mark. A business's customer data is used only for that business and never joined across businesses (RULES 4.10), so a person who is a customer of two businesses has two rows. The person, their handles, their phone row with the stopped flag, and the paused flag are K-04's; a yes to texts is a K-29 consent row; a block is a customer_blocks row.
tables.source: FS line 727 (customer); RULES 4.8, 4.10; S13-19; S13-45; A4-23, B4-25 ('A new customer is added to the business's customer list once booked'); A3-30, B3-08; 02-contracts section 7 row K-28 and section 8 (customer, reach_by)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The customer row's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09). Later parts name a customer by it (FS lines 737, 738: a membership's and a pack's customer_id).
columns.source: FS line 727 (id); CQ-09

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business whose customer list it is on (businesses.id). Row-level security scopes by it, so no other business reads it (RULES 4.10).
columns.source: FS line 727 (business_id); RULES 4.10; arch 10 line 546

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person (persons.id), as K-04's booking head names a booker, person served or payer. Their role at this business is K-04's person_roles row with role customer, which the guard lists (arch 02 line 115); this row is that customer's record at the business, not a second role.
columns.source: FS line 743 ('A person is one row'); K-04 v1 persons, person_roles; arch 02 line 115

columns.name: name
columns.description: The name this business has on file for them: as their own AI sent it (A4-23, B4-25) or as the business booked them (A3-19: 'BOOK Alex M. haircut Sat 11am Riley'; B3-08: 'BOOK Tessa drain Thu 12-2 Casey'). A record on file is linked to a new conversation only when a proven contact and the name they type match (S13-45). Kept per business and never copied from or to another business's record (RULES 4.10); K-04's persons.name is the person's own name across Rosie. Plain, as persons.name (K-04 v1 rule 6). Texts about a child, or for sensitive work, show it only as RULES 4.6 and 4.7 allow (the claim check, limit 7).

columns.name: mobile_handle_id
columns.description: Their mobile on file: the handle (handles.id) of a K-04 phones row, and one of their own handles (person_handles). Texts go to it when their way is texts or textsonly. The number, its chat, its Linq contact (Q-03: added when it is saved) and its stopped flag across every business (MC C1) are that K-04 handle's and phone row's, never repeated here. Required when the customer or their own AI books (MC C2; D103), which the reach card checks (A4-82, B4-93); null for a customer the business booked with no mobile (A3-19: 'A customer with no mobile can be booked too'), or once staff took the number off in person (S13-19). A switch of where updates go moves it to the new contact (RULES 9.1).
columns.source: FS line 727 (mobile, required when the customer or their own AI books); MC C1, C2; D103; Q-03; A4-82, B4-93; A3-19; S13-19; RULES 9.1

columns.name: email_handle_id
columns.description: Their email on file: a K-04 handle (handles.id) of kind email, and one of their own handles (person_handles). Optional (MC C2: 'an email stays optional and gets every message'); it gets every message in step with the chat (RULES 4.1, 4.8), and everything when their way is email. The address itself is the K-04 handle's. A lost phone's code goes only to it (RULES 9.2b). Null: none given.
columns.source: FS line 727 (email, optional); MC C2; D103; RULES 4.1, 4.8, 9.2b; A4-82, B4-93

columns.name: way
columns.description: How Rosie reaches them, from the reach card (A4-82, B4-93) or the owner's read-back (A3-30, B3-08): texts, textsonly or email, spelt as K-01 v1's bookingValues.reach. Calls only is not offered (Q-07; MC C2), and textsonly works like texts while there is no voice (Q-07). Every message goes this way, fallbacks too (S13-19), and an email on file also gets every message (RULES 4.8). A change on the same contact is set at once on their word in their own chat (A7-98: 'Calls instead of texts, or quiet times, on the same number: set at once'). Null only when no contact is on file: Rosie then sends them nothing, and the business reaches them its own way (S13-19).
columns.source: FS line 727 (reach way); RULES 4.8; S13-19; A4-82, B4-93; A3-30, B3-08; A7-98; Q-07; MC C2; K-01 v1 bookingValues.reach; 02-contracts section 8 (reach_by)

columns.name: contact_times
columns.description: The times they named for being reached, in their own words as read back (S13-19: 'Contact preferences: the person served sets how and when they're reached. That's the way, the times, first name only and no voicemail'; A3-50: 'Weekdays after 6pm'). The owner and staff line of a private booking says to reach them only at these times (S13-19). Kept as their words: no source gives a form code can read (README, open gaps). Null: none named.
columns.source: FS line 727 (contact preferences: times); S13-19; A3-50, B3-32

columns.name: first_name_only
columns.description: They asked to be named by first name only (S13-19; A3-50, B3-32): messages about them and the business's own calls use their first name only.
columns.source: FS line 727 (contact preferences: first name only); S13-19; A3-50, B3-32

columns.name: no_voicemail
columns.description: They asked for no voicemail (S13-19; A3-50, B3-32): nobody leaves one. Rosie places no calls (Q-05), so it binds the business's own person.
columns.source: FS line 727 (contact preferences: no voicemail); S13-19; A3-50, B3-32; Q-05

columns.name: age_band
columns.description: Their answer to 'are you 18 or older?' (A4-80, B4-92), or the age the read-back of a booking the business adds gave (A3-30, B3-08: 'For Tessa, 18 or older'): 18_or_older or under_18, never an exact age (A4-80: 'Never ask a child's exact age'). The question is skipped only for a record whose phone was proven in an earlier booking and that says 18_or_older, and only for that record's own person (A4-80: 'Someone new on the same phone is asked their age'); under_18 is asked again. Nothing is kept about a child under 13 or a teen booking alone (A4-80; RULES 4.7). Staff see it because Sam, a barber or the desk books for a customer, and the read-back they answer carries the age their reply sets (A3-19, A3-30). under_18 is a child's detail, which no staff or owner text carries (RULES 4.5; RULES 4.7: 'Staff and owner texts name only the parent and the time or class'), so for them the claim check (limit 7) treats it as secure-page-only. Null: not asked.

columns.name: fee_free
columns.description: The owner marked them fee-free on the Customers page (S11-57; FS section 6.2): they are never asked a late-cancel or no-show fee (S11-22). Never used or hinted at before the one rule proves the contact (S13-45: 'no fee-free label'). The reasons stay K-26's notes (K-26 v1 README).
columns.source: FS line 727 (fee_free); S11-57; S11-22; S13-45; FS section 6.2 (Customers)

columns.name: added_at
columns.description: When the business's list gained them: once booked (A4-23, B4-25), or when the business booked them (A3-30, B3-08).
columns.source: A4-23, B4-25 ('A new customer is added to the business's customer list once booked'); A3-30, B3-08

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: customers_business_person_key
unique.source: FS line 727 (business_id); RULES 4.10 (one record per person at each business)

checks.name: customers_way_known
checks.expression: way is null or way in ('texts', 'textsonly', 'email')
checks.source: Q-07 (calls only is not offered); MC C2; K-01 v1 bookingValues.reach

checks.name: customers_way_fits_contact
checks.expression: ((way is null) = (mobile_handle_id is null and email_handle_id is null)) and (way <> 'email' or email_handle_id is not null) and (way not in ('texts', 'textsonly') or mobile_handle_id is not null)
checks.source: A4-82, B4-93 ('so the branch always fits the line'); S13-19

checks.name: customers_age_band_known
checks.expression: age_band is null or age_band in ('under_18', '18_or_older')
checks.source: A4-80, B4-92 ('are you 18 or older?'; 'Never ask a child's exact age')

indexes.name: customers_mobile_idx
indexes.why: The business's record on file for a proven mobile (S13-45; 02-contracts K-09 v1.1, journey 3: 'find or add the customer by mobile'), and K-26's own-customers rule (FS K10).

indexes.name: customers_email_idx
indexes.why: The business's record on file for a proven email (S13-45; RULES 9.2b).

indexes.name: customers_person_idx
indexes.why: A person's records, for the runtime side's jobs that work by person, such as the 45-day copy or delete (RULES 4.10); no business scope reads another business's row.

tables.name: customer_blocks
tables.description: A business's block of one customer, by their number or by their address for home visits (S11-62: 'Sam blocks a number, or an address for home visits, by telling the AI or in the portal'; FS section 6.2, Customers). While it holds, AI assistants and the booking page hear only that the business can't take their booking, with no reason given. One row per block; lifting keeps the row (S11-62: 'Sam can lift the block at any time'; 'Rosie's team sees each block, in case it's a mistake'). FS line 727's blocked is whether an open row exists. Not K-04's pauses: a pause holds visits for the owner's decision (A3-48), a block refuses new bookings.
tables.source: S11-62; FS line 727 (blocked); FS section 6.2 (Customers: 'block a number or an address'); 02-contracts section 7 row K-28 ('blocked number or address (S11-62)')

columns.name: id
columns.description: The block's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business that blocked (businesses.id): a block holds only at that business. Row-level security scopes by it.
columns.source: S11-62; arch 10 line 546

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person blocked (persons.id). They need no customer row at the business: Sam may block a first-time sender whose threat booked nothing (A3-48, B3-30: 'Paused until you decide: keep them paused, or block them'), and a customer row comes only once booked (A4-23), so a block adds none. A number block's handle is one of their own (customer_blocks_phone_own_fk), and their key seals an address block's address (arch 01 line 93).
columns.source: S11-62 ('Blocks a customer'); A3-48, B3-30; A4-23; arch 01 line 93

columns.name: target
columns.description: number or address: 'Sam blocks a number, or an address for home visits' (S11-62).
columns.source: S11-62; FS section 6.2 (Customers)

columns.name: phone_handle_id
columns.description: For a number: the blocked mobile, the handle (handles.id) of a K-04 phones row and one of the customer's own handles (person_handles). A new booking that gives it, through their own AI, the booking page or a text, hears only that the business can't take it (S11-62).
columns.source: S11-62 ('Sam blocks a number'; 'AI assistants hear that the business can't take their booking, with no reason given')

columns.name: address
columns.description: For an address: the street address for home visits, sealed under the key of the person in person_id, as K-04's pauses.address (K-04 v1 rule 6; arch 01 line 93), so deleting their key erases it. Never in a text, an email or to an AI (RULES 4.5): shown only on a secure, signed-in page, the owner's Customers page. A flow B booking's address is checked against the business's open address blocks in code, after unsealing them.
columns.source: S11-62 ('an address for home visits'); arch 01 line 93; RULES 4.5, 4.10; K-04 v1 pauses.address

columns.name: set_at
columns.description: When the block was set.

columns.name: set_by_person_id
columns.description: Who set it (persons.id): the account owner, or an admin the owner lets (RULES 6.8; S13-45 row 8). Whether that person may is K-22's.

columns.name: set_by_turn_id
columns.description: The turn that set it (turns.id), when the owner told the AI; null when it was set in the portal (S11-62: 'by telling the AI or in the portal').
columns.source: S11-62; K-04 v1 turns

columns.name: lifted_at
columns.description: When it was lifted; null while it holds (S11-62: 'Sam can lift the block at any time').

columns.name: lifted_by_person_id
columns.description: Who lifted it (persons.id).

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: customer_blocks_one_open_number
unique.source: S11-62 (a number is blocked at a business, or it is not)

checks.name: customer_blocks_target_known
checks.source: S11-62 ('a number, or an address for home visits')

checks.name: customer_blocks_one_target
checks.expression: (target <> 'number' or (phone_handle_id is not null and address is null)) and (target <> 'address' or (address is not null and phone_handle_id is null))

checks.name: customer_blocks_lifted_together
checks.source: S11-62 ('Sam can lift the block at any time')

checks.name: customer_blocks_lifted_after_set
checks.expression: lifted_at is null or lifted_at >= set_at

indexes.name: customer_blocks_customer_idx
indexes.why: A customer's blocks, for the Customers page and the read-back that names any plan, membership or credits a block ends (S11-62).

indexes.name: customer_blocks_open_address_idx
indexes.why: A flow B booking's address is checked against the business's open address blocks (S11-62).
